title: Mini SDK Pod Connector — Quickstart and Canonical Fallbacks
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

This page describes a compact, production-minded quickstart for the "Mini SDK Pod Connector" — a small, well-instrumented SDK-side adapter designed for constrained or ephemeral compute (edge VMs, IoT gateways, mobile background workers). The connector provides:

- A lightweight HTTP/WebSocket facade to Redwood's API that enforces local telemetry and retry contracts.
- Deterministic fallbacks: local cache, synchronous stub, and degraded-mode output (short responses).
- Packaging guidance for serverless/ephemeral runtimes (single binary or minimal container).
- Docs site and snippet lifecycle guidance so examples remain runnable in our docs playground.

Goals

1. Make it easy to run a small SDK integration in low-memory/low-network environments.
2. Provide canonical retry/telemetry contracts for support teams to debug quickly.
3. Ship examples that are testable by docs automation and maintained with the docs pipeline.

Who should use this

- Integrations engineers building small adapters for customer environments (edge, on-prem gateways).
- SDK maintainers who need a reproducible lightweight runtime to run integration tests.
- Support engineers who want a deterministic set of fallbacks to reproduce customer issues.

Prerequisites

- Redwood API key with read/write generation scopes (dev key OK for local testing).
- Docker (for local container quickstart) or Go 1.20+ / Rust 1.70+ toolchain if building native binary.
- Optional: docs-playground VM access for automated snippet testing.

Quickstart: Containerized connector (recommended)

1) Clone the template repo

   git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/mini-pod-connector-template.git
   cd mini-pod-connector-template

2) Copy credentials for local testing (dev only)

   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-dev-xxx

3) Build and run the container

   docker build -t mini-pod-connector:local .
   docker run -p 8080:8080 -e REDWOOD_API_KEY -e ENV=local mini-pod-connector:local

4) Healthcheck and sample request

   curl http://localhost:8080/health
   # expected: {"status":"ok","uptime":"PT0S"}

   curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"Summarize: Redwood Inference","max_tokens":40}'

Architecture and responsibilities

- HTTP facade (port 8080): handles auth, local cache, telemetry, and request shaping.
- Upstream client: handles calls to Redwood API with batching awareness.
- Telemetry agent: emits per-request events to our telemetry sink and local file for offline debugging.
- Fallback engine: ordered list — 1) cached KV prefix; 2) local stub JSON; 3) short canned summary.

API examples (connector facade)

1) Generation POST (simple)

   POST /v1/generate
   Body: {"prompt":"string","max_tokens":int,"temperature":float}

   Sample response: {"id":"conn-req-01","status":"ok","tokens":33,"result":"..."}

2) Streaming via WebSocket (forwarding mode)

   ws://localhost:8080/v1/stream?session=abc123
   - Client sends single JSON open frame with {"prompt":"...","mode":"stream"}
   - Connector upgrades, streams events from Redwood's streaming endpoint and emits standard events: event: token, event: end, event: error

Implementation snippets

- Outbound request example (pseudo-shell):

   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"prompt":"%PROMPT%","max_tokens":%MAX%}'

- Local cache policy (YAML example inserted into connector config):

   cache:
     type: lru
     size: 1000
     ttl_seconds: 3600

Telemetry contract (canonical fields)

We standardize the local telemetry emitted by the connector so support and docs pipelines can rely on fixed keys. The connector must emit the following JSON-lines to STDOUT and to the telemetry sink (when available):

| field | type | description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| trace_id | string | UUID V4 per external request |
| connector_id | string | pod instance id (hostname or generated id) |
| upstream_model | string | model name used upstream (e.g., redwood/gpt-8-small) |
| phase | string | one of [incoming, cache_hit, upstream_call, fallback, stream_chunk, completed, error] |
| latency_ms | integer | round-trip time for upstream call (ms), present when phase=upstream_call |
| error_code | string | structured error tag for canonical fixes (optional) |

Packaging and runtime guidance

- Single-binary preference: static linking (Go/Rust) reduces cold-starts. Keep image base minimal (distroless).
- Memory target: <=150MB resident for default config. Use streaming to avoid buffering.
- Configuration precedence: env vars > mounted config file > built-in defaults.

Docs site integration and snippet lifecycle

- All code snippets used on the public docs site must be runnable by the docs playground harness. To achieve this:
  1. Keep snippets under 200 lines and avoid local secrets.
  2. Provide a minimal Dockerfile and a Health endpoint for the playground to validate.
  3. Include a small test YAML manifest: tests/doc-playground.yml that runs a simple generate request.

- When updating connector examples, add an entry to docs-site/snippet-registry with: snippet id, Docker image tag, healthcheck path, and test command. The CI docs job will run the snippet and report failures.

Canonical support issues and fixes (top patterns)

1) Symptom: Connector returns 503 with error_code "upstream_backpressure"
   - Root cause: connector batch queue is full because the upstream client has slow tokens.
   - Canonical fix: increase local batch_size (config) OR enable direct-pass-through mode for latency-sensitive routes.
   - Command to gather logs: 
     journalctl -u mini-pod-connector --since "1 hour ago" | grep "trace_id=<TRACE>"

2) Symptom: Local stub returned instead of upstream content (phase=fallback)
   - Root cause: upstream auth failed (expired key) or networking egress blocked.
   - Canonical fix: validate REDWOOD_API_KEY env var and test direct curl to api.redwood.ai.
   - Diagnostic curl: 
     curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models

3) Symptom: Streaming stops mid-response (phase=stream_chunk, then error)
   - Root cause: idle timeouts on intermediary proxies or keepalive not negotiated.
   - Canonical fix: enable ping frames on client websocket; set connector keepalive to 30s; set proxy max idle to 90s.

4) Symptom: High token counts and cost anomalies
   - Root cause: client sent unbounded prompts or connector failed to enforce per-request max_tokens.
   - Canonical fix: set per-route max_tokens and enable token-usage tracing.
   - Config sample: {"routes":{"/v1/generate":{"max_tokens":256}}}

Debugging checklist (ordered)

1. Reproduce locally with the provided mini-pod-connector:local image and the failing input.
2. Collect connector logs for trace_id and telemetry lines.
3. Run upstream curl test to validate egress and credentials.
4. If streaming issue, capture pcap of websocket frames between client and connector.
5. If cost spike, query token summary from connector telemetry and cross-check with usage dashboard in Redwood Console.

Rollout and upgrade guidance

- Canary deploy: deploy 5% of connectors to new image tag with a traffic mirror. Observe: 95th percentile latency, cache hit rate, and fallback rate for 48 hours.
- Auto-rollback: trigger when fallback_rate > 0.5% for the canary slice or when error budget breaches for >30 minutes.

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (sdk-integration team) — contact: Ava Patel (ava@redwood.ai)
- Support escalation: customer-success (level-1) -> eng-sre (level-2).

Appendix A — Example connector config (minimal)

   connector_id: mini-1
   listen_port: 8080
   upstream_url: https://api.redwood.ai
   cache:
     enabled: true
     type: lru
     ttl_seconds: 3600
   routes:
     "/v1/generate":
       max_tokens: 256
       allow_streaming: true

Appendix B — Test commands for docs CI

- Healthcheck: 
  curl -sf http://mini-pod-connector:8080/health || exit 1

- Smoke generate test: 
  curl -s -X POST http://mini-pod-connector:8080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":10}' | jq '.status=="ok"'

Notes and follow-ups

- We keep the connector intentionally small to make debugging repeatable. For heavy workloads prefer Redwood Dedicated or a full SDK.
- Consider adding an integration test that replays captured telemetry traces against new connector releases.

If you have questions or need a walkthrough for a specific customer environment, contact the owner listed above.
